examples.worked_solution:
We can write $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot [\begin{aligned}24 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}v\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}) = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathbf{v},$ we conclude that the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k = \dfrac{1}{4}.$

Remember that the matrix representing a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060608/assets/4866597a50fbdb530e9275c77f2ca926c932c7cc334635bd05191aaddd510d75.png)

Therefore, the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ is
